title: Between the Queens: the five stages from the 600-cell to the 120-cell, with their slices and shadows
description:
Version 2 adds short cross-references to later results: the three uniform members of the 600-cell × 120-cell sweep of #91 are the cuts of Proposition 1; the two ends and every stage are spherical 11-designs, with a 19-design, found numerically, on the path (Section 2); the walls and the hidden shapes of #110 and of Alicia in Wonderland, Chapters 10 and 11 (Sections 1, 2 and 4); the midpoint's truncated icosahedra (Section 4). It uses the regular names 600-cell and 120-cell in the text, with Schläfli's credit and DICTO's names in a note, and one credit line for the computation.

In #63 the 600-cell* (Schläfli, 1852) is mapped, and in #65 the 120-cell** (Schläfli, 1852) is built exactly from it. The four-dimensional icosahedron with hexagons, and the stages that lead from the one to the other, are DICTO's ideas. Cut the 600-cell's corners, deeper and deeper, and it passes through five uniform four-dimensional solids before it becomes the 120-cell: the truncated and rectified 600-cell, the bitruncated 600-cell (the midpoint, whose cells are 120 truncated icosahedra and 600 truncated tetrahedra), and the rectified and truncated 120-cell. All seven are classical: Alicia Boole Stott was the first to list the semiregular four-dimensional solids, in 1910, and they are Wythoff's and Coxeter's uniform polytopes. We build each stage from the 600-cell's own corners, edges, triangles and cells, prove the cut positions that make every edge equal (1/3, 1/2, 3/5, the triangle centre and (5 − √5)/10), and give the complete atlas of their slices and shadows in the four directions of #63 and #65: 1402 slices from the centre to the tips, and 20 shadows. Main theorem: the numbers of slices and the shadows of Table 2, with both ends equal to the exact atlases of #63 and #65; and in every direction the shadows of the truncated and the rectified 600-cell have the same number of faces, and so do those of the rectified and the truncated 120-cell. The stages are in the app: a slider in the 600-cell's world runs from the 600-cell to the 120-cell.

Computation, proofs, verification and drafting with Claude (Anthropic).
